ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anytime semantic segmentation by warping a past frame's features with event-derived motion
PROPOSAL: We encode the last RGB frame into dense semantic features once, estimate a continuous-time motion field from the event stream up to the query time with a recurrent event encoder conditioned on the target offset, and warp the frame features to that time before a light decoder predicts the semantic map. Only past and current events are used, so the method is causal, and the offset input makes it answer at any time inside the interval. We evaluate on driving datasets with paired events and labels, synthesising intermediate labels by interpolation where needed.
CONTROLS: Copying the last frame's segmentation, event-only segmentation, RGB-event fusion at the frame time, and a video interpolation method given the future frame as an upper reference.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Accuracy should decay slowly with offset and stay well above the copied segmentation at long offsets. Newly appearing objects not visible in the last frame may be missed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Building anytime labels for the interval between low-rate frames
PROPOSAL: We construct an evaluation set for causal anytime segmentation by recording driving scenes with a high-rate camera and an event camera together, labelling the high-rate frames with a strong segmentation model followed by human correction, and then keeping only every tenth frame as model input. This yields dense ground truth at many offsets inside each interval, including scenes with sudden pedestrian crossings and vehicles cutting in.
CONTROLS: Agreement between two human correctors on a subset, comparison of the automatic labels with fully manual labels on a sample, and a check that event timestamps align with high-rate frames within the sensor tolerance.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The dataset should expose a steady loss of accuracy with offset for frame-based methods. Label noise at object boundaries may limit how finely methods can be ranked.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fusing static context and sparse events with offset-conditioned cross-attention
PROPOSAL: We fuse a frozen image backbone's features from the last frame with a sparse event representation accumulated up to the query time, using cross-attention in which the event tokens query the image tokens and the time offset is added as a learned embedding. A decoder then outputs the semantic map at the queried time. We train on driving and drone sequences with labels at several offsets and test on intervals longer than seen in training.
CONTROLS: Concatenation fusion with the same backbones, event-only and image-only models, and the fused model without the offset embedding.
COST: 380
PREDICTION: Cross-attention fusion should beat concatenation at long offsets and in fast scenes. Offsets longer than seen in training may expose poor extrapolation of the offset embedding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Handling occlusion and newly appearing objects in the blind interval
PROPOSAL: We add a second branch to an image and event segmentation model that predicts from events alone the regions where the warped image context is no longer valid, such as areas uncovered by moving objects or newly entering objects, and blends in an event-only prediction there. We evaluate separately on pixels that keep, lose or gain an object after the last frame.
CONTROLS: The model without the validity branch, a blending rule based on event density alone, and the copied last-frame segmentation, all split by pixel category.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The validity branch should improve accuracy on newly appearing objects while leaving stable regions unchanged. Slow-moving objects that produce few events may not be detected as new.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness of anytime segmentation to event noise and low light
PROPOSAL: We stress causal image and event segmentation models with sensor noise, low light, flicker and rain, using recordings under those conditions and simulated noise at controlled rates, and measure how accuracy at different offsets degrades. We also test a denoising front end trained on the same event statistics.
CONTROLS: Clean daytime recordings as reference, image-only prediction under the same conditions, and the model with and without the denoising front end.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Event noise should hurt long offsets the most, since more events accumulate before the query. The denoising front end should recover part of the loss, but flicker may remain hard.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency and power of anytime segmentation on embedded hardware
PROPOSAL: We deploy an image and event anytime segmentation network on an embedded accelerator of the kind used on drones and small robots and measure latency per query, energy per query, and the highest query rate it sustains while the camera runs at its native low rate. We compare it with running a frame-based model on a high-speed camera at the same effective rate.
CONTROLS: The frame-based model at native camera rate, the same network with the offset branch disabled, and an event-only network of similar size.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The image and event network should sustain high query rates at a small fraction of the energy of the high-speed camera pipeline. Memory traffic for image features may dominate energy on small devices.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-supervised training for anytime segmentation without intermediate labels
PROPOSAL: We train an anytime segmentation model without labels inside the interval by predicting the segmentation of the next frame from the current frame and events, and by enforcing temporal consistency between predictions at nearby offsets. The labels of the next frame come from a strong frame segmenter. We test whether this self-supervised scheme matches training on dense intermediate labels.
CONTROLS: Training with dense intermediate labels, training with next-frame supervision only, and copying the last frame's segmentation.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Next-frame supervision plus consistency should approach the dense-label model at short and middle offsets. Without intermediate supervision, mid-interval predictions may lag behind fast objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of anytime segmentation from driving to legged robots and drones
PROPOSAL: We train an image and event anytime segmentation model on driving data and test it, with and without short fine-tuning, on recordings from a quadruped robot and a drone, which have very different motion patterns and viewpoints. We measure accuracy across offsets and analyse which classes fail to transfer.
CONTROLS: Models trained on the target platform from scratch, the copied last-frame segmentation, and event-only models on each platform.
COST: 280
PREDICTION: Static classes such as road and building should transfer well, while moving classes may need fine-tuning. Drone viewpoints may cause the largest drop.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How long can the blind interval grow before predictions fail
PROPOSAL: We train and evaluate causal image and event segmentation with intervals between frames increased stepwise, from a short gap to one several times longer, to find the interval at which accuracy falls below that of a high-rate frame pipeline. We report accuracy against offset for each interval and for scenes of different speed.
CONTROLS: A frame-based model at a high frame rate as reference, the copied last-frame segmentation, and the same model trained only at the shortest interval.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Accuracy should remain close to the high-rate reference for short intervals and degrade beyond a speed-dependent limit. Fast scenes should reach that limit earliest.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event representations for continuous-time semantic prediction
PROPOSAL: We compare voxel grids, time surfaces, learned point-based encodings and spiking encoders as the event input to a single anytime segmentation architecture, keeping the image branch and decoder fixed, and measure accuracy, latency and robustness at all offsets.
CONTROLS: The image-only model, the copied segmentation, and each event representation at two temporal resolutions.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Point-based encodings should give the best accuracy at long offsets, while voxel grids should be fastest. Spiking encoders may trail on accuracy but excel on energy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Causal anytime segmentation from one frame and events, tested inside the blind interval
PROPOSAL: We warp dense features from the last frame to any query time with a motion field estimated causally from events and decode a semantic map, and test whether this stays accurate across the whole interval. Evaluation uses dense labels at many offsets from a high-rate reference camera, so the claim is checked where frames are missing.
CONTROLS: Copying the last frame's segmentation, event-only segmentation, fusion at the frame time only, a video interpolation method that sees the future frame as a non-causal upper reference, accuracy reported per offset bin, and a split by object speed.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Accuracy should stay well above the copied segmentation at long offsets and close to interpolation at short ones. A large gap at long offsets would show motion estimation fails there.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Causal anytime segmentation from one frame and events in driving scenes
PROPOSAL: We warp dense features from the last frame to any query time with a motion field estimated causally from events and decode a semantic map. We train the model on driving sequences and report mean intersection over union on the labelled frames of the dataset, which arrive at the low camera rate.
CONTROLS: Two event voxel resolutions, two backbone depths, a comparison of two optimisers, an ablation of the decoder width, a check that the model runs in real time on one accelerator, and segmentation maps for a few sequences rendered side by side with the camera image.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The model should reach high intersection over union on the labelled frames. Small classes such as poles may stay hard.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does offset-conditioned cross-attention fusion help at long offsets
PROPOSAL: We fuse last-frame image features with events accumulated to the query time through cross-attention conditioned on the time offset, and ask whether this fusion improves accuracy deep in the interval, where context from the frame has aged.
CONTROLS: Concatenation fusion with the same backbones, the fused model without offset conditioning, image-only and event-only models, the copied segmentation, dense labels at many offsets from a high-rate reference camera, and results split by offset and by scene speed over three seeds.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Conditioned cross-attention should lead concatenation most at long offsets and in fast scenes. No gain beyond short offsets would show that the offset input is not used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-conditioned cross-attention for fusing images and events
PROPOSAL: We fuse last-frame image features with events accumulated to the query time through cross-attention conditioned on the time offset, and describe the design of the attention blocks and how training behaves on driving and drone sequences.
CONTROLS: Two numbers of attention heads, two token sizes for the event branch, an ablation of positional encodings, the model trained with and without mixed precision, loss curves for each variant, and attention maps for a few sample scenes plotted over the input image.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The attention blocks should learn to focus on moving regions. More heads may give slightly sharper maps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Newly appearing and occluded objects in anytime segmentation
PROPOSAL: We add a validity branch that predicts from events where the warped frame context no longer holds and blends an event-only prediction there, and we test it on the pixels that matter for safety: those that gain or lose an object after the last frame.
CONTROLS: The model without the branch, a blending rule from event density alone, the copied segmentation, accuracy split into stable, revealed and newly occupied pixels, a held-out set of sudden pedestrian crossings, and three seeds with intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The branch should raise accuracy on newly occupied pixels without hurting stable ones. Gains only on stable pixels would mean the branch does not address appearance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A validity branch for blending event-only predictions into warped context
PROPOSAL: We add a validity branch that predicts from events where the warped frame context no longer holds and blends an event-only prediction there, and report overall mean intersection over union on driving test sequences along with the branch's average activation.
CONTROLS: Two loss weights for the branch, two blending functions, the branch placed at two decoder depths, an ablation of its normalisation layers, the overall score for each variant, and visualised validity masks for a few frames.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The branch should slightly raise the overall score. Validity masks should concentrate on moving vehicles.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-supervised anytime segmentation checked against dense intermediate labels
PROPOSAL: We train with next-frame supervision and temporal consistency between nearby offsets, needing no labels inside the interval, and test whether this matches models trained with dense intermediate labels across the interval.
CONTROLS: A model trained with dense intermediate labels as reference, next-frame supervision without consistency, consistency without next-frame supervision, the copied segmentation, dense test labels at many offsets from a high-rate camera, and per-offset accuracy with three seeds.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The self-supervised model should approach dense supervision at short and middle offsets. A large gap at mid-interval would show that consistency does not replace intermediate labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-supervised training for segmentation between low-rate frames
PROPOSAL: We train with next-frame supervision and temporal consistency between nearby offsets, needing no labels inside the interval, and report the score on the next labelled frame together with the training curve for each loss term.
CONTROLS: Two weights on the consistency term, two sampling schemes for offsets during training, an ablation of data augmentation, the model trained on half the sequences, the score on the next frame, and sample predictions at several offsets for qualitative review.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The model should match a supervised model on the next labelled frame. Consistency may stabilise training curves.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Limits of the blind interval for causal image and event segmentation
PROPOSAL: We lengthen the interval between input frames stepwise and find, for scenes of different speed, the offset at which causal image and event segmentation falls below a high-rate frame pipeline, which tells how far perception can be decoupled from frame rate.
CONTROLS: A frame model run at high rate as reference, the copied segmentation, the model trained only on the shortest interval, dense labels at all offsets, results split by scene speed, and confidence intervals from three seeds.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Slow scenes should tolerate long intervals and fast ones should hit the limit early. If the model stays close to the reference everywhere, the test lacks hard scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training image and event segmentation at several frame intervals
PROPOSAL: We lengthen the interval between input frames stepwise and train causal image and event segmentation at each length, reporting the score on the labelled frames and the training time needed for each interval.
CONTROLS: Two event window sizes, two learning-rate schedules, an ablation of the temporal encoder depth, models trained on the day and night subsets apart, the score on the labelled frames for each interval, and memory use during training.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Longer intervals should need longer training to reach a stable score on the labelled frames, since the temporal encoder sees more events per sample. Night sequences may train more slowly than day ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuous-time segmentation by warping frame context with event motion
PROPOSAL: We encode the last frame once, estimate a continuous motion field from events up to any query time with an offset-conditioned recurrent encoder, warp the frame features to that time, and decode a semantic map, using no future frame. This targets the gap directly: dense semantics at any moment between two slow frames.
CONTROLS: Copied segmentation, event-only and image-only models, fusion at the frame time, and a non-causal interpolation reference.
COST: 380
PREDICTION: Accuracy should decay slowly with offset. Objects appearing after the last frame may be missed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-based reconstruction of intensity frames followed by segmentation
PROPOSAL: We reconstruct intensity images from the event stream at a high fixed rate with a recurrent reconstruction network, and run a standard frame segmenter on each reconstructed image, using no future frame. This aims at the gap by producing frames where the camera gives none, though only at the fixed reconstruction times.
CONTROLS: Copied segmentation, event-only and image-only models, fusion at the frame time, and a non-causal interpolation reference.
COST: 380
PREDICTION: Segmentation of reconstructed images should beat the copied map. Reconstructions may lose texture and blur small classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fusing a single frame with the event stream for any query time
PROPOSAL: We merge the static semantic context of the last frame with the sparse event stream through cross-attention whose queries are event tokens and whose conditioning is the time offset, producing a semantic map at any requested time within the interval. We test on dynamic driving scenes and on long intervals.
CONTROLS: Concatenation fusion, image-only and event-only models, the copied segmentation, and per-offset accuracy.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: Fusion should beat both single-modality models at all offsets. Very long intervals may still degrade.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving segmentation of the current frame with past events
PROPOSAL: We merge the semantic context of the current frame with events from the preceding interval through cross-attention, so that motion cues sharpen object boundaries and help in low light, producing a better segmentation at the frame time itself. We test on dynamic driving scenes and on night sequences.
CONTROLS: Concatenation fusion, image-only and event-only models, existing enhancement methods, and accuracy at the frame time.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: Fusion should beat the image-only model, especially at night. Gains may be small in well-lit scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training anytime segmentation without intermediate labels
PROPOSAL: We supervise predictions at the next frame with labels from a strong frame segmenter and enforce temporal consistency between predictions at nearby offsets, so that a causal model learns to answer at any time without dense labels inside the interval. We evaluate on dense labels at many offsets from a high-rate camera.
CONTROLS: Dense-label training, next-frame only, consistency only, and the copied segmentation.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The scheme should approach dense supervision at short offsets. Mid-interval accuracy may lag for fast objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training frame interpolation networks for driving video
PROPOSAL: We train a video interpolation network that takes two consecutive frames and the events between them to synthesise intermediate frames, and then segment those frames with a strong frame segmenter, so that semantic maps become available between camera frames. We evaluate on dense labels at many offsets from a high-rate camera.
CONTROLS: Dense-label training, frame-only interpolation, event-only reconstruction, and the copied segmentation.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Interpolated frames should give accurate maps at all offsets. The method needs the next frame before it can produce output.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anytime image and event segmentation on embedded platforms
PROPOSAL: We deploy a causal anytime segmentation network on an embedded accelerator used by drones and small robots and measure whether it can answer at high query rates with low latency and power while the camera runs at its slow native rate, which is what decoupling perception from frame rate requires in practice.
CONTROLS: A frame model on a high-speed camera at the same effective rate, an event-only network, and per-query latency and energy.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: The network should sustain high query rates at low energy. Memory traffic may limit small devices.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compressing frame segmentation networks for embedded platforms
PROPOSAL: We prune and quantise a frame segmentation network for an embedded accelerator used by drones and small robots, so that it runs at the camera's slow native rate with lower latency and power, and measure how accuracy at the frame times changes with compression level.
CONTROLS: The uncompressed network, a smaller network trained from scratch, an event-only network, and per-frame latency and energy.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Moderate compression should keep accuracy while halving latency. Strong quantisation may hurt thin classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anytime segmentation across driving, legged and aerial platforms
PROPOSAL: We train a causal image and event anytime segmentation model on driving data and test it on quadruped and drone recordings with dense labels inside the interval, to see whether high-rate semantic perception from slow cameras holds beyond cars. We analyse per-class accuracy against offset on each platform.
CONTROLS: Per-platform models, the copied segmentation, event-only models, and short fine-tuning.
COST: 290
PREDICTION: Static classes should transfer while moving ones need tuning. Drone viewpoints may hurt most, since their scale and motion differ from road scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-platform frame segmentation datasets for robots
PROPOSAL: We assemble a multi-platform segmentation dataset of driving, quadruped and drone recordings labelled at the camera frame rate, and benchmark frame segmenters trained on one platform and tested on the others, to see how semantic perception from slow cameras holds beyond cars. We analyse per-class accuracy on each platform.
CONTROLS: Per-platform models, models trained on all platforms, event-only models, and short fine-tuning.
COST: 290
PREDICTION: Road and building classes should transfer while others need tuning. Drone imagery may differ most, since its altitude and framing are far from cars.
